title: Tool install and enable control plane: make missing tools repairable and gated features one-click configurable
goal: AegisPT must ship with all software-based pentest tool groups installable by the official installer and container image. Settings must not leave operators at vague degraded/blocked labels: each missing software tool group needs a clear Install/Repair path, and each disabled-but-supported capability needs a safe Enable/Configure action that preserves scope, ROE, approval gates, pack registry, deployment, runtime binding, and kill-switch controls.
scope: Operator feedback 2026-05-03: Settings reports degraded/blocked states and optional tools not installed, but does not provide a clear way to fix them. Product direction: software tooling should be installed/prepared by default where host permissions allow; risky capabilities may remain disabled until explicitly enabled, but they must be visible and enableable through governed controls.
generation_reason: Operators need AegisPT to be complete after install: all software tools prepared, risky features disabled/gated rather than absent, and Settings must expose actionable repair/enable controls.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Install/repair and enablement UX only. Do not auto-run pentest tools, do not auto-enable intrusive execution, and do not bypass authorization, approval, scope, pack validation, deployment, runtime binding, or kill-switch controls.

success_criteria: Official host installer and Compose image include all tracked software tool groups where packages are available: Nmap, Nuclei, httpx, ZAP, Responder, NetExec, BloodHound, Impacket, Metasploit, Hashcat, SNMP, and WiFi analysis tooling.
Readiness detection accepts the actual command names installed and used by AegisPT runners, including Impacket `.py` commands and any compatibility aliases.
Settings shows each degraded software tool group with a concrete Install/Repair action or copyable privileged command, including exact expected binaries and affected assessment families.
Settings distinguishes software-missing from hardware-missing. WiFi software can be ready while wireless adapter hardware remains blocked until attached.

Disabled but supported capabilities expose an Enable/Configure button that writes governed settings only; execution still requires the existing ROE, scope, approval, deployment, runtime binding, and kill-switch controls.
A post-install verification artifact proves all software tool groups are ready on a supported host image or clearly records privilege/hardware blockers.
No pentest tool is executed against a live target as part of installation or enablement.
must_not_touch: Pack registry, validation, deployment, or runtime binding flows

required_checks: bash scripts/verify_host.sh or documented privilege-safe equivalent on a prepared host
acceptance_criteria: Readiness reports software tool groups ready on the prepared host or records exact install blockers.
Settings exposes actionable install/repair/enable controls instead of vague degraded text.
Hardware-only blockers remain honest and separate from software installation gaps.

after_completion: Promote exactly one next approved task into NEXT_TASK.md.

out_of_scope: Enabling intrusive execution without operator authorization
Installing WiFi hardware or drivers that require manual host passthrough
